accuracy.evidence: Speech punctuation follows the Oxford/New Hart's rules and the KS2-3 grammar glossary: spoken words inside inverted commas; punctuation belonging to the speech (comma, question mark) inside the closing mark; a comma replaces the full stop before a reporting clause; the reporting clause after speech starts lower case (Mia whispered, Leo asked); a new paragraph for each new speaker, with a character's own action beat kept in their paragraph (lab step 2: Gran's 'She lifted it gently' stays, Leo's action beat starts his turn). The craft advice (prefer said or an action beat to adverb tags; distinct voices; reflective conclusion per CCSS W.8.3.e) is stated as craft advice, not as a rule, and matches Browne and King and King's On Writing. Numeric items (paragraph and speech-mark counts) were checked at the corners of their ranges.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented KS3 dialogue errors: full stop before the tag (step 1 prediction, gap feedback, challenge 'stop', p1), comma outside the closing mark (gap feedback, challenge 'outside', p1), question mark placement (gap b0 feedback, m1), one block for a whole conversation or a new paragraph per sentence (step 2, challenge 'scene' and 'every', m2), adverb and fancy tags (step 3 prediction, challenge 'adverb' and 'fancy', m3), naming feelings flatly (challenge 'tell', p3), same-sounding characters (step 4, challenge 'same' and 'tagall', m4) and dream or twist endings (step 5 prediction, challenge 'dream' and 'twist', p5, m8).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagdlg works on the mechanics and craft of dialogue itself: placing punctuation tokens into the gaps of a spoken line, inserting paragraph breaks in a block of speech, swapping adverb tags for action beats, and attributing untagged lines to a speaker by voice. flagpace (narrative pacing, filler dialogue), flagmentor (show/tell in a mentor text, planning a character) and flagplot (story mountain, character arc) have none of these. lab_distinct gate passes under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner meets each rule by trying it: a wrong mark in a gap is refused with the reason, the block of speech only reads clearly once each speaker gets a ¶, the action-beat line is chosen against the adverb line three times with the feeling named each time, and the six untagged lines can only be matched by noticing sentence length and word choice, which is the point about voice. The text then confirms the rule in one sentence.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: 'a full stop, because her words end there' (the gap refuses the full stop and explains why the sentence goes on), 'Gran said nervously' as more believable (the action beat is the one accepted), and 'It was all a dream' as a stronger ending (the dream card is rejected as cancelling the story).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions with eleven distinct wrong-answer messages: stop, outside, scene, every, adverb, tell, tagall, same, dream, twist and fancy, each naming the slip (for example 'The comma belongs inside the closing speech mark, next to the spoken words').

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and name each term with an example (speech marks, tag, action beat, voice, reflective ending) and pass the kid readability limit; the adult text uses the curriculum terms inverted commas, reporting clause, characterisation and reflective conclusion within the adult limit. Canvas cards hold one line of dialogue each and wrap cleanly on a phone.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean. Each kid paragraph teaches one convention or craft move; each item checks a different point: punctuation (p1, m1), paragraph count (p2, p4), showing (p3, m6), reflective ending (p5, m8), new-speaker rule (m2), tags (m3), voice (m4), speech-mark count (m5), an opening with setting, point of view and hook (m7) and cutting dialogue that repeats the narrator (m9).

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android light and dark and iPhone 13 dark screenshots of every step at start, mid-demo and after Show me: the two speech lines wrap with 28 px gaps that do not overlap the words; five 52 px punctuation tiles fit in one row; seven dialogue rows fit with the ¶ marker and indent; the paired tell/show cards, the dealt line above two voice boxes and five endings all fit without clipping. Canvas drag of a token onto the gap and of a line onto a voice box was tested on iPhone 13 emulation.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: each punctuation mark ('Put a comma in the gap'), 'New paragraph before: …' for each line, both tag versions, both speakers and each ending. The canvas aria-label is rewritten with every feedback message. walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors.
